# Attention Widgets: A Study of Focused Retrieval

## Abstract

We study whether structure-aware retrieval over a document's own
table of contents beats flat chunking. ABSTRACT_MARKER: the abstract
summarises the whole paper in four sentences.

## Introduction

Flat chunking destroys document structure: a 1,000-character window
does not know which section it came from. INTRODUCTION_MARKER: this
section motivates section-addressed retrieval.

## Methods

We ran a within-subjects study on section addressing.
METHODS_MARKER: the methods overview describes the design before the
subsections below split it into participants and procedure.

### Participants

PARTICIPANTS_MARKER: forty-two volunteer readers took part, each
reading three papers and answering section-targeted questions.

### Procedure

PROCEDURE_MARKER: each reader was timed while locating the section
that answered a question, using either flat chunks or the tree.

## Results

RESULTS_MARKER: leaf-title addressing located the correct section in
91 percent of trials, against 54 percent for flat chunk retrieval.

## Discussion

DISCUSSION_MARKER: the gains concentrate on queries that name a
section, which is exactly the case flat chunking handles worst.
